messages.author: d0591fb2a98d1e44
messages.subject: Positive Semidefinite restriction
parts: I'm thinking of using RStan to do some quantum mechanics and a requirement is that the operators be positive semidefinite matrices. Therefore, I was wondering if it is it possible to require that a parameter (which is a matrix) is positive semidefinite? Also, is Stan capable of dealing with complex values (ex. 1+i)?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Positive Semidefinite restriction
parts:
You can declare a cov_matrix parameter, which will be symmetric and positive definite even if you are not actually using it as a covariance matrix. Stan doesn't do complex values so you would have to compute the real and imaginary parts separately.

Ben

doesn't have any native sort for imaginary numbers.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Positive Semidefinite restriction
parts:
On Thursday, June 4, 2015 at 10:43:55 PM UTC-4, Daniel Berman wrote:
Given that I want to place constraints on the matrix such as positive semidefiniteness, is that still possible?

If you were interested in the complex matrix A where

A = B + i * C

and both B and C are real, symmetric, and positive semi-definite, then maybe something could be done with Stan but you would have to deal with the real and imaginary parts separately. See, e.g.,

http://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/~higham/narep/narep298.pdf

More generally, for any sort of a constrained multivariate unknown, Stan needs a mapping between that space and the real numbers. And Stan doesn't have any such mappings built in for complex variables.

Ben

On Thursday, June 4, 2015 at 9:59:02 PM UTC-4, Andrew Gelman wrote:
You can just express such a matrix as two matrices, one for the real part and one for the imaginary part, and then just carry thru all the math in that way, working out the real and imaginary parts using the appropriate formulas.  I suppose it should be possible to write Stan functions to do these.
